experiences.name: Street Food Tour in Centro Histórico
experiences.description: Explore the bustling streets of Mexico City's historic center sampling iconic local dishes such as tacos de canasta, tlayudas, tamales, and churros from legendary street vendors and traditional markets like Mercado San Juan.

experiences.name: Visit the National Museum of Anthropology
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Mexico's rich pre-Hispanic heritage at one of the world's greatest museums, featuring the famous Aztec Sun Stone, Mayan artifacts, and exhibits spanning thousands of years of Mesoamerican civilization.

experiences.name: Xochimilco Trajinera Canal Ride & Local Food
experiences.description: Float through the ancient Aztec canals on a colorful trajinera boat while enjoying freshly prepared local food from passing vendors, including elotes, quesadillas, and micheladas — a vibrant cultural and culinary experience unique to Mexico City.

experiences.name: Coyoacán Neighborhood Walk & Frida Kahlo Museum
experiences.description: Stroll through the charming cobblestone streets of Coyoacán, visit the iconic Casa Azul (Frida Kahlo Museum), browse artisan markets, and enjoy local snacks like tostadas and aguas frescas in this bohemian cultural hub.

experiences.name: Mercado de la Merced Culinary Exploration
experiences.description: Dive deep into one of Mexico City's largest and most authentic traditional markets, tasting regional specialties like mole negro, pozole, memelas, and exotic fruits while interacting with local vendors and learning about indigenous ingredients.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Check in to your boutique stay in Centro Histórico after landing and settling in.
day_by_day.afternoon: After check-in, take a leisurely walk to the iconic Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest city squares in the world. Explore the exterior of the Palacio Nacional and the stunning Metropolitan Cathedral — both free to admire from outside. Wander through the surrounding streets to soak in the historic atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Calle Regina, a vibrant pedestrian street just minutes from your hotel, filled with street performers, local vendors, and a lively neighborhood vibe. Visit the nearby Plaza Garibaldi area for a taste of mariachi culture.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport before landing or grab a quick snack from a street vendor near the hotel upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Mercado San Juan (a short walk from Centro) — try affordable tacos or tortas from market stalls for around 40–80 MXN.
meals.dinner: Tacos de canasta on Calle Regina or a local taquería near the Zócalo — budget-friendly tacos for 15–25 MXN each. Try tacos de guisado for an authentic local experience.

day_by_day.notes: Keep your first afternoon light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Exchange currency at a reputable casa de cambio (avoid airport rates). Metro and walking are your best budget transport options in Centro.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Templo Mayor archaeological site (entry ~80 MXN), the ruins of the ancient Aztec capital Tenochtitlán, located just steps from the Zócalo. Explore the on-site museum included in the ticket price — allow 2 to 3 hours for a thorough visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Palacio de Bellas Artes to admire its stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco exterior and the free murals visible in the lobby. Then walk through Alameda Central park, Mexico City's oldest public park, perfect for people-watching. Nearby, visit the Museo de Arte Popular (entry ~60 MXN) to discover vibrant Mexican folk art and crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Barrio Chino (Chinatown) on Calle Dolores, just a short walk from Alameda. Browse street food stalls and enjoy the eclectic mix of Mexican and Chinese flavors at very low prices.

meals.breakfast: Café de chino or a local fonda near your hotel — chilaquiles or huevos a la mexicana with coffee for around 60–90 MXN.
meals.lunch: Mercado de Artesanías or a nearby comida corrida (set lunch menu) restaurant — a full 3-course meal typically costs 80–120 MXN and is one of the best budget deals in the city.
meals.dinner: Street tacos or quesadillas from a night market stall near Alameda Central — budget 80–120 MXN total.

day_by_day.notes: Sunday entry to Templo Mayor and many national museums is free for Mexican nationals but still charges tourists the standard fee. Arrive at Templo Mayor early to beat crowds. Comfortable walking shoes are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro (Line 2, ~5 MXN per ride) to Coyoacán neighborhood. Visit the Frida Kahlo Museum — Casa Azul (entry ~270 MXN, book online in advance as tickets sell out). This iconic blue house is a must-see for culture lovers and offers deep insight into Mexican art and history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming Coyoacán neighborhood on foot — browse the Mercado de Artesanías de Coyoacán for affordable souvenirs and handicrafts. Visit the Jardín Centenario and Plaza Hidalgo, the lively heart of Coyoacán with street performers and local vendors.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico via Metro. Visit the rooftop terrace of a nearby building or take an evening walk along Madero Street, one of the most beautiful pedestrian boulevards in the city, beautifully lit at night.

meals.breakfast: Grab a tamale and atole (warm corn-based drink) from a street cart near the hotel — a classic Mexico City breakfast for under 40 MXN.
meals.lunch: Mercado de Coyoacán food stalls — try tostadas de tinga, enchiladas, or pozole for 50–100 MXN. This market is famous for its affordable, delicious local food.
meals.dinner: Comida corrida at a local fonda back in Centro Histórico or a bowl of sopa de lima and tostadas — budget 80–130 MXN.

day_by_day.notes: Book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets at least 2–3 weeks in advance online — walk-in availability is extremely limited. The Metro is the cheapest and fastest way to reach Coyoacán. Avoid rush hour (7–9am, 6–8pm) if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Teotihuacán, the ancient city of pyramids (about 50 km from Centro). Take a bus from Terminal Central del Norte (Metro Line 5 to Autobuses del Norte station, then a bus to Teotihuacán for ~50 MXN each way). Entry to the archaeological zone is ~80 MXN. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon for breathtaking views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Avenue of the Dead and the Temple of Quetzalcoatl within the Teotihuacán complex. Browse local artisan vendors at the site entrance for affordable obsidian crafts and souvenirs. Head back to Mexico City by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax and recover with a quiet evening in Centro. Walk to Plaza Santo Domingo, a quieter and more authentic square than the Zócalo, surrounded by colonial architecture and local life.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departing — grab pan dulce (sweet bread) and café de olla from a street cart or panadería near your hotel for under 30 MXN.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks or buy food from vendors at the Teotihuacán site — quesadillas and grilled corn (elote) are available for 30–60 MXN. Alternatively, eat at a simple restaurant near the entrance for ~120–150 MXN.
meals.dinner: Back in Centro, try pozole or birria from a local restaurant near the Zócalo — a hearty and warming meal for 80–130 MXN.

day_by_day.notes: Depart early (by 8am) to make the most of Teotihuacán before it gets crowded and hot. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water — the site is largely open with little shade. Wear sturdy shoes for climbing the pyramids. The round trip including entry costs roughly 180–200 MXN total — extremely budget-friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec (entry ~85 MXN) — one of the greatest museums in the world, housing extraordinary collections of Aztec, Maya, and other pre-Columbian artifacts including the famous Aztec Sun Stone. Allow at least 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Bosque de Chapultepec (Chapultepec Forest), one of the largest urban parks in the world — entry is free. Rent a rowboat on the lake (~60 MXN), relax on the grass, or visit the free Galería de Historia museum within the park. This is a beloved local hangout and a great place to observe everyday Mexico City life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro for a final evening of exploration. Visit the Mercado de la Ciudadela for last-minute artisan shopping and affordable souvenirs. End your trip with a farewell dinner at a traditional cantina or pulquería to try pulque, Mexico's ancient fermented agave drink.

meals.breakfast: Full Mexican breakfast at a local fonda near your hotel — eggs, beans, tortillas, and coffee for 70–100 MXN. A satisfying send-off meal.
meals.lunch: Street food near Chapultepec — elotes, tlayudas, or tacos from vendors along the park perimeter for 50–80 MXN.
meals.dinner: Traditional cantina near Centro Histórico — try chiles en nogada (seasonal), mole negro, or enchiladas verdes with a glass of pulque or agua fresca. Budget 120–180 MXN for a full, satisfying farewell meal.

day_by_day.notes: The Museo Nacional de Antropología is free on Sundays for Mexican nationals but charges tourists the standard fee on all days. If your flight departs on Day 6, pack your bags tonight and confirm transport to the airport. Mexico City's Metro is the cheapest airport transport option (Line 5 to Terminal Aérea station) for around 5 MXN, though it does not serve Terminal 2 — check your terminal in advance.

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer from airport to boutique hotel in Centro Histórico. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely walk around the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), Mexico City's massive main square. Visit the exterior of the Palacio Nacional and the Metropolitan Cathedral. Stroll through the historic streets to soak in the colonial architecture and street life.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the pedestrian street of Madero, browse local shops, and head to the Alameda Central park for a relaxing evening stroll. Enjoy the illuminated fountains and people-watch as the city comes alive at night.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pan dulce at the hotel or a nearby panadería upon settling in.
meals.lunch: Café de Tacuba — a historic restaurant just steps from the Zócalo serving traditional Mexican dishes like enchiladas and pozole in a stunning 1912 setting. Mid-range pricing.
meals.dinner: El Cardenal (Centro branch) — beloved local institution known for authentic Mexican cuisine including tamales, mole, and seasonal specialties. Budget around 300–450 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 begins after 13:00 arrival. Keep the afternoon light to recover from travel. Exchange currency or use ATMs near the hotel for local pesos.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Palacio Nacional to see Diego Rivera's iconic murals depicting Mexican history — free entry. Then head to the Templo Mayor archaeological site and museum, the ruins of the ancient Aztec capital Tenochtitlán, located right next to the Zócalo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Barrio de Tepito market area or visit the Mercado de Artesanías La Ciudadela for authentic crafts, textiles, and souvenirs. Afterward, walk to the charming neighborhood of San Juan and browse Mercado de San Juan for gourmet local and international products.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the lively Plaza Garibaldi to hear the famous Mariachi bands perform live — a quintessential Mexico City experience. The square fills with energy after dark.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local fonda near the hotel — try chilaquiles rojos or huevos rancheros with fresh-squeezed orange juice. Budget around 80–120 MXN.
meals.lunch: Mercado de San Juan food stalls — try freshly prepared tacos, tlayudas, or seafood tostadas from market vendors. Authentic and affordable at 100–180 MXN.
meals.dinner: Restaurant near Plaza Garibaldi such as Salón Tenampa — enjoy traditional Mexican food and drinks while Mariachis serenade your table. Budget 350–500 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Palacio Nacional is free. Templo Mayor entry is approximately 85 MXN. Wear comfortable walking shoes — this is a high-step day. Keep valuables secure in crowded markets.

day_by_day.morning: Take a metro or Uber to Coyoacán neighborhood. Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo (Casa Azul) — book tickets in advance online. Explore the colorful colonial streets, murals, and bohemian atmosphere of this beloved barrio.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Mercado de Coyoacán for lunch, then visit the nearby Museo León Trotsky (former home of the exiled Russian revolutionary). Continue to Viveros de Coyoacán, a beautiful public park and nature reserve, for a relaxing afternoon walk.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico or venture to the trendy Roma Norte neighborhood for dinner and evening drinks. Explore the tree-lined streets, art galleries, and café culture of Roma.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Café El Jarocho in Coyoacán — a legendary local café famous for its rich Mexican coffee and simple pastries. Iconic and very affordable.
meals.lunch: Mercado de Coyoacán food stalls — try tostadas de tinga or enfrijoladas from local vendors. One of the best casual food experiences in the city. 100–160 MXN.
meals.dinner: Contramar (Roma Norte) or a similar mid-range Mexican seafood spot — known for fresh fish tacos and creative Mexican dishes. Budget 400–600 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Museo Frida Kahlo tickets online well in advance — they sell out frequently. Coyoacán is about 30–40 minutes from Centro by Uber (150–200 MXN each way) or accessible by metro (Line 3 to Viveros).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Teotihuacán — one of the most impressive ancient sites in the Americas. Take an early Uber or organized shuttle to arrive before the midday heat. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon, and walk the Avenue of the Dead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Teotihuacán, including the Temple of Quetzalcóatl and the site museum. Return to Mexico City by mid-to-late afternoon. Stop at a local mezcalería or pulquería near the hotel to decompress and taste traditional Mexican spirits.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nightlife and dining scene of Centro Histórico. Visit the rooftop bar of a nearby hotel for panoramic views of the Zócalo lit up at night — a stunning sight.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or grab tamales and atole from a street vendor near the hotel before departure — a classic Mexican morning meal.
meals.lunch: La Gruta restaurant at Teotihuacán — a unique dining experience inside a natural cave near the archaeological site. Traditional Mexican set menus. Budget 350–500 MXN per person.
meals.dinner: Azul Histórico in Centro Histórico — beautiful courtyard restaurant serving refined regional Mexican cuisine. Budget 400–600 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Depart for Teotihuacán by 8:00–8:30 AM to beat crowds and heat. Entry fee is approximately 95 MXN. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water — the site is very exposed. Uber to Teotihuacán costs approximately 350–500 MXN each way.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec — one of the world's greatest museums, housing extraordinary collections of pre-Columbian art and artifacts including the famous Aztec Sun Stone. Spend 2–3 hours exploring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Bosque de Chapultepec, Mexico City's vast urban forest and park. Visit Chapultepec Castle (Castillo de Chapultepec) for panoramic city views and exhibits on Mexican history. Browse the park's vendors and enjoy the relaxed local atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening — return to Centro Histórico for a farewell dinner. Take a last walk around the Zócalo, pick up any remaining souvenirs, and reflect on the trip over drinks at a local cantina.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at a neighborhood café in Centro — try molletes (toasted bolillo with beans and cheese) or a classic Mexican breakfast spread. 100–150 MXN.
meals.lunch: Lunch near Chapultepec in Polanco neighborhood — try Mercado Artz food hall or a casual taquería on the streets of Polanco for a mid-range meal. 200–350 MXN.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Los Girasoles in Centro Histórico — elegant yet accessible Mexican restaurant with a wide menu of traditional dishes and good mezcal selection. Budget 400–600 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Museo Nacional de Antropología entry is approximately 85 MXN — free on Sundays for Mexican nationals. Chapultepec Castle entry is approximately 85 MXN. Both are reachable via metro (Chapultepec station, Line 1) or Uber from Centro (100–150 MXN).

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private transfer from Aeropuerto Internacional Benito Juárez to your boutique hotel in Centro Histórico via luxury chauffeur service. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided walking tour of the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), the second-largest public square in the world. Visit the imposing Catedral Metropolitana and admire the exterior of the Palacio Nacional, home to Diego Rivera's legendary murals. Stroll through the surrounding colonial streets with your expert local guide.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on a rooftop bar overlooking the illuminated Zócalo — try Bar El Mayor or the rooftop of the Gran Hotel Ciudad de México for breathtaking views. Followed by a refined dinner at a celebrated Centro Histórico restaurant.

meals.lunch: Light welcome meal at the hotel or a nearby upscale café such as Café de Tacuba, a historic institution serving traditional Mexican dishes since 1912
meals.dinner: Dinner at Azul Histórico — an elegant courtyard restaurant inside a colonial mansion, renowned for elevated regional Mexican cuisine and artisanal mezcal pairings

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Keep the first afternoon leisurely to recover from travel. Confirm hotel concierge can book all subsequent restaurant reservations upon check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Templo Mayor archaeological site and its world-class museum, exploring the ancient Aztec ceremonial center at the heart of Tenochtitlán. Your expert archaeologist guide will bring the layers of history to life. Afterward, browse the artisan galleries along Calle Moneda.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive visit to the Palacio de Bellas Artes to admire its stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture, Diego Rivera and David Siqueiros murals, and rotating fine art exhibitions. Then take a short walk to the Palacio Postal (Correo Mayor), one of the most ornate buildings in Latin America. End with a leisurely stroll through the Alameda Central gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Private mezcal and tequila tasting experience led by a certified sommelier at a curated mezcalería in the Juárez or Roma neighborhood, featuring rare single-origin spirits and traditional botanas (snacks). Followed by an intimate dinner at one of Mexico City's most acclaimed fine-dining establishments.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent breakfast at the hotel — order from the à la carte menu featuring chilaquiles, fresh tropical fruits, and Mexican pastries (pan dulce)
meals.lunch: Lunch at El Cardenal near Palacio de Bellas Artes — a legendary restaurant celebrated for its authentic, home-style Mexican cooking and exceptional mole dishes
meals.dinner: Dinner at Quintonil — one of Latin America's 50 Best Restaurants, Chef Jorge Vallejo's tasting menu showcases indigenous Mexican ingredients in extraordinary contemporary preparations

day_by_day.notes: Book Quintonil well in advance (weeks ahead if possible). Templo Mayor opens at 9:00 AM — arrive early for a quieter experience. Wear comfortable shoes for extensive walking.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day excursion to the ancient pyramids of Teotihuacán (approximately 50 km northeast of the city). Arrive early via luxury chauffeured vehicle to beat the crowds. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon with a private archaeologist guide. Explore the Avenue of the Dead and the Temple of Quetzalcóatl.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and check into the experience of a traditional temazcal (pre-Hispanic steam ceremony) at a luxury spa — many five-star hotels and wellness centers in Polanco or Roma offer this authentic ritual. Alternatively, visit the stunning Museo Franz Mayer, a premier decorative arts museum housed in a 16th-century hospital.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the upscale Polanco neighborhood — a short taxi or Uber ride from Centro. Browse the luxury boutiques along Presidente Masaryk Avenue before settling in for a landmark dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before departure — fresh juices, yogurt, and pastries to prepare for the pyramid climb
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic prepared by your hotel or a stop at La Gruta, a dramatic restaurant set inside a natural cave at the Teotihuacán site
meals.dinner: Dinner at Pujol — Chef Enrique Olvera's iconic flagship, consistently ranked among the world's best restaurants. The legendary 'Mole Madre' aged mole dish is unmissable. Tasting menu format with optional wine or mezcal pairing

day_by_day.notes: Depart for Teotihuacán by 7:30 AM to arrive at opening time and avoid midday heat and crowds. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and comfortable walking shoes. Pujol reservations are essential and should be booked weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private art and culture tour of the Coyoacán neighborhood — the bohemian heart of Mexico City. Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo (Casa Azul), the iconic blue house where the legendary artist was born and lived. Pre-book a private early-access slot to avoid crowds. Explore the colorful Coyoacán market for local flavors and handicrafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby Anahuacalli Museum, Diego Rivera's extraordinary lava-stone pyramid-temple housing his vast collection of pre-Columbian artifacts. Then head to the San Ángel neighborhood for a walk through its cobblestone streets, colonial mansions, and the famous Bazar del Sábado artisan market area (or the permanent galleries nearby). Stop at the Museo Casa Estudio Diego Rivera y Frida Kahlo.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico or head to the trendy Roma Norte neighborhood for a curated progressive dinner — start with craft cocktails at a speakeasy-style bar, followed by a multi-course dinner at a celebrated chef's table experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café in Coyoacán — try Café El Jarocho, a beloved neighborhood institution, for strong Mexican coffee and fresh tamales
meals.lunch: Lunch at Los Danzantes in Coyoacán — a sophisticated restaurant with a beautiful courtyard, specializing in Oaxacan cuisine and an extensive mezcal library
meals.dinner: Dinner at Rosetta in Roma Norte — Chef Elena Reygadas' celebrated restaurant in a converted mansion, blending Italian influences with Mexican ingredients. Exceptional housemade pasta and seasonal tasting menus

day_by_day.notes: Frida Kahlo Museum requires advance ticket booking — private early access slots sell out quickly. Allow 45 minutes travel time between Centro Histórico and Coyoacán. Consider hiring a private driver for the day given the distances involved.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive private Mexican cooking class with a celebrated local chef — learn to make traditional dishes from scratch including handmade tortillas, mole negro, and agua fresca. Classes are often held in beautiful historic kitchens in Centro or Roma and include a market visit to source fresh ingredients at Mercado de San Juan, Mexico City's premier gourmet market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely final afternoon — explore the Museo Nacional de Arte (MUNAL) for an outstanding collection of Mexican fine art spanning five centuries, housed in a stunning neoclassical building near the Zócalo. Followed by a private shopping experience for high-end Mexican crafts, textiles, and artisanal goods at curated boutiques in Centro Histórico such as those along Calle Madero or inside the historic Casa de los Azulejos.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — a memorable final meal celebrating the best of Mexico City's culinary scene, followed by a nightcap at a sophisticated rooftop bar with panoramic city views.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — splurge on the full Mexican spread: enfrijoladas, fresh-squeezed juices, tamales, and artisanal coffee
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes prepared during your morning cooking class as part of the experience — a truly personal and authentic meal
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Contramar in Roma Norte — one of Mexico City's most beloved and iconic restaurants, famous for its signature tuna tostadas and grilled fish al pastor. Vibrant, celebratory atmosphere perfect for a final evening. End the night with cocktails at Balcón del Zócalo rooftop bar

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class through a premium provider such as 'Eat Mexico' or via hotel concierge for a private chef experience. Confirm departure logistics and arrange luxury airport transfer for the following morning if needed. Allow time for any last-minute souvenir shopping at Mercado de San Juan.
